proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly gives Bengali jāoyā, Assamese zāiba, Oriya jibā, Bihari/Maithili jāeb, Old Marwari jāvaï and Gujarati jāvũ under yāti go. These whole survey j-/dz- nonpast or infinitive forms fit those regional stems and endings. Past g- forms are assigned separately to gata; negative prefixes and complex responses are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Turner identifies Hindi gayā, Nepali/Kumaoni gayo and Old Gujarati gyau/giu as suppletive preterites of go from gata. These survey gV(y)- forms preserve that gone/past stem even though the elicitation gloss is simply go. Forms retaining an l expansion are assigned to the separate *gatailla branch.
